intro: Welcome to the İzmir Archaeology Museum, in İzmir province, founded in 1927. Here the finds of the Smyrna agora meet those of the Ionian cities around it, such as Klazomenai and Teos. And watch for the faces: the museum is known for its collection of Roman portrait sculpture.
history: The museum was founded in 1927, and in 1984 it moved to its present building in Bahribaba Park. Its collection comes from the excavations of İzmir and the Ionian cities around it — Smyrna, Klazomenai, Teos and Bayraklı. Its strongest holdings are Roman portrait sculpture and the statuary of the Smyrna agora.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Roman portraits, the finds from the Smyrna agora, the coin collection and, outside, the stone garden.
facts: Did you know? The core of the collection comes from the Smyrna agora excavations, including its statues of Poseidon and Demeter. Those two statues belong to the rebuilding of the city after the earthquake of AD 178, paid for with imperial help. And the museum gathers the finds of the Ionian cities around İzmir — Klazomenai, Teos and Bayraklı — under one roof.
outro: This brings our tour of the İzmir Archaeology Museum to an end. Before you go, please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These faces have looked out across the centuries; let them keep looking for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
